question: Map the chain from a Semiconductor market requirement to a measurable parameter and then to a required capability of Oscilloscope.
answer: The Vault supports the chain only qualitatively, in two traceable variants. (1) High-speed digital / SerDes: the R&S high-speed-digital source (0 Digital Test – What are SIPI and Serdes, cover date 2026.3.4) frames the semiconductor-side requirement as the validation challenges of high-speed electrical interfaces (Tx/Rx, channel, Tx/Rx packages, PCBs, connectors); the measurable parameters named are eye diagram, IL (insertion loss), Xtalk (crosstalk) and TDR impedance in the "Signal integrity flow of high speed PCB/PCBA", plus the Power Distribution Network block; and the required instrument capability is scopes — the concept page maps "Interface Test" and "Power Distribution Network" to [[Oscilloscope]] (with BERTs/AWGs/switch matrices and network analyzers respectively). (2) Power-semiconductor / PMIC: the market driver recorded is the 800V high-voltage architecture upgrade and the AI-server claim that "Blackwell platform power consumption doubles, driving high-density power demand"; the measurable parameters are power rail, multiphase DC and power integrity (with PDN Target Z assigned to R&S ZNL); and the mapped instrument is MXO for power rail / multiphase DC / PI. Both chains stop at instrument *type*: the Vault explicitly records that no model, bandwidth, data rate or test standard is given for the scopes, no PDN impedance target value or method, and no option/firmware/fixture/calibration conditions for MXO. There is also no [[Oscilloscope]] (or MXO/RTO) entity page in the Vault, so no oscilloscope specification can be cited — only the functional role. Note that for the explicitly semiconductor rows of the AI-server mapping (IC/IP, test interface, high-speed transmission IC) the Vault maps VNA and FSWP, not an oscilloscope.
missing: The Vault supports only a qualitative chain. It lacks: (a) any numeric target or pass/fail threshold for the measurable parameters (no eye-diagram mask, IL/Xtalk limits, PDN impedance target value or measurement method, no jitter mask); (b) any oscilloscope specification — there is no [[Oscilloscope]], MXO, RTO or RTP entity page, hence no bandwidth, sample rate, channel count, probe or option data from which a 'required capability' could be derived (the source pages state model/bandwidth/data-rate/standard are not provided); (c) an explicit statement that MXO/RTO are oscilloscopes (only R&S RTO6 is labelled 'Oscilloscope', and that is in an O-RU energy-saving context, not semiconductor); (d) a direct link from the explicitly semiconductor rows (IC/IP design, test interface/probe, high-speed transmission IC) to an oscilloscope — those rows map to ZNA/ZNA67EXT/FSWP instead.

key_points.point: The semiconductor-side market/engineering requirement is recorded as the validation challenge of high-speed electrical interfaces (Slide 11 of the R&S high-speed digital source, cover date 2026.3.4).
key_points.source: wiki/concepts/SerDes 與 SI PI 測試概覽.md
key_points.quote: 在 Slide 11 以 **Transmission Channel and validation challenges electrical Interfaces** 描述高速電性介面的驗證挑戰

key_points.point: The measurable parameters in that chain are eye diagram, IL, Xtalk and TDR impedance, listed in the signal-integrity flow for high-speed PCB/PCBA.

key_points.quote: Slide 20 題為 **Signal integrity flow of high speed PCB/PCBA**，列出 [[IL]] / [[Xtalk]] / [[Eye diagram]]、[[TDR Impedance]]

key_points.point: The required instrument capability for Interface Test is scopes (oscilloscopes), alongside BERTs, AWGs and switch matrices; the Power Distribution Network block maps to scopes and network analyzers.

key_points.quote: 未提供型號、頻寬、資料率或測試標準

key_points.point: A second chain runs from the power-semiconductor market driver (800V high-voltage architecture upgrade) on the semiconductor side.

key_points.point: The instrument-side link is a sales mapping without test conditions: no option, firmware, fixture or calibration conditions are given for MXO (nor for ZNL/FSWP/ZNA).
